answer_text:
Let

\[
G = F/N.
\]

Since \(N\) is the normal subgroup generated by \(a^3\), \(b^2\), and \(aba^{-1}b^{-1}\), the quotient \(G\) has the presentation

\[
G=\langle a,b \mid a^3=1,\ b^2=1,\ aba^{-1}b^{-1}=1\rangle.
\]

The relation

\[
aba^{-1}b^{-1}=1
\]

implies

\[
ab=ba,
\]

so \(G\) is abelian. Therefore every element of \(G\) can be written in the form

\[
a^i b^j.
\]

Using the relations \(a^3=1\) and \(b^2=1\), we may reduce exponents to

\[
0\le i\le 2,\qquad 0\le j\le 1.
\]

Thus

\[
|G|\le 3\cdot 2=6.
\]

To see that there are exactly \(6\) elements, observe that the cyclic group \(C_6=\langle g\mid g^6=1\rangle\) satisfies the same relations by taking

\[
a=g^2,\qquad b=g^3.
\]

Here \(a\) has order \(3\), \(b\) has order \(2\), and \(a\) and \(b\) commute. Moreover, \(a\) and \(b\) together generate \(C_6\). Hence \(G\) maps onto \(C_6\), so

\[
|G|\ge 6.
\]

Therefore,

\[
|G|=6.
\]

Since \([F:N]=|F/N|=|G|\), the index is

\[
\boxed{6}.
\]
